assertions.assertion: Problem statement names what decides the right payment (litres converted from the meter unit, at the co-op rate; month by dairy local time) and says the paid amount can differ, so one pickup or farm-month could confirm or refute it
assertions.evidence: The hypothesis says: "A pickup's payment depends on its litres (converted from the meter unit) and on the month it happened at the dairy. Some pickups are paid on a different amount or put in a different month." It doesn't name the rate, but it states the deciding rules in general terms and says payments can differ from them, which can be checked one pickup at a time.

assertions.assertion: The problem statement does not build in a cause or fix (e.g. gallons paid as litres, UTC date, multiply by 3.785)
assertions.evidence: The statement gives only the rules: convert from the meter unit, and use the month at the dairy. The causes ("the code ignores `unit`", "uses the UTC date") and the 3.785/UTC-7 figures appear only later, under Findings, as evidence.

assertions.assertion: Both complaints fit the problem statement and the statement can fail (names a falsifier or the facts fixing the right amount)
assertions.evidence: F-07's wrong amount and F-12's month misplacement both fit "paid on a different amount or put in a different month." The statement names its own falsifier: "This would be false if every pickup's payment and month matched those rules."
